name: Proto-Indo-European
blurb: The unwritten mother tongue of most of Europe and much of Asia, spoken on the Pontic–Caspian steppe. Linguists rebuild it by comparing its descendants.

name: Proto-Afroasiatic
blurb: The deep ancestor of Arabic, Hebrew, Egyptian and Berber.

name: Proto-Germanic
blurb: Ancestor of English, German, Dutch and the Scandinavian languages, spoken around the North Sea and the Baltic.

name: Old English
blurb: Brought to Britain by Angles, Saxons and Jutes. Most of our everyday words — water, bread, love, house — come straight from it.

name: Middle English
blurb: The English of Chaucer: Old English reshaped by Norse and flooded with French.

name: English
blurb: Modern English: a magpie language with the largest vocabulary on Earth, still growing by thousands of words a year.

name: Scots
blurb: English's northern sibling, home of bonny, glamour and wee.

name: Frankish
blurb: The Germanic language of the Franks; it lent French — and so English — words like guard, war and blue.

name: Old Norse
blurb: The language of the Vikings, who settled the Danelaw. Gave English sky, egg, knife, window and even they.

name: Icelandic
blurb: Old Norse's most faithful descendant: geyser and saga.

name: Swedish
blurb: Gave English smorgasbord, ombudsman and tungsten.

name: Norwegian
blurb: Gave English ski, slalom, fjord and lemming.

name: Middle Dutch
blurb: Language of the Flemish cloth trade.

name: Dutch
blurb: Sailors and traders gave English yacht, boss, cookie, landscape and sketch.

name: Middle Low German
blurb: Lingua franca of the Hanseatic League.

name: German
blurb: Gave English kindergarten, angst, hamster, wanderlust and noodle.

name: Yiddish
blurb: Brought to English by Jewish immigrants: glitch, schmooze, chutzpah, bagel.

name: Afrikaans
blurb: Gave English aardvark, trek and apartheid.

name: Gothic
blurb: The earliest Germanic language with books.

name: Latin
blurb: The language of Rome, and of the Church, law and science for 1,500 years afterwards. Directly or via French, perhaps 60% of English words trace back to it.

name: Vulgar Latin
blurb: The everyday spoken Latin that became French, Spanish and Italian.

name: Medieval Latin
blurb: The Latin of monks, universities and lawyers.

name: New Latin
blurb: Scholarly Latin of the scientific revolution: virus, species, formula, Homo sapiens.

name: Old French
blurb: Spoken across northern France in the age of chivalry.

name: Anglo-Norman
blurb: The French of England's rulers after 1066 — the language of court, castle and courtroom.

name: French
blurb: Modern French gave English ballet, cuisine, café, déjà vu and rendezvous.

name: Old Occitan
blurb: The language of the troubadours.

name: Ancient Greek
blurb: Homer, Plato and Hippocrates. English borrowed it for ideas and science: philosophy, democracy, atom, -ology.

name: Koine Greek
blurb: The Greek of the New Testament.

name: Gaulish
blurb: Celtic language of Gaul; its words reached English through Latin and French (car, carpenter).

name: Irish
blurb: Gave English galore, smithereens, brogue and shamrock.

name: Scottish Gaelic
blurb: Gave English clan, slogan, glen, bog and whisky.

name: Welsh
blurb: Gave English corgi, penguin (probably) and flannel.

name: Breton
blurb: Gave English menhir and dolmen.

name: Italian
blurb: Music, art, banking and food: piano, opera, fresco, bank, pizza.

name: Spanish
blurb: Brought words from Spain and the Americas: canyon, guitar, mosquito, tornado.

name: Portuguese
blurb: Sailors' words from four continents: marmalade, cobra, flamingo.

name: Akkadian
blurb: Language of Babylon and Assyria, written in cuneiform.

name: Aramaic
blurb: Lingua franca of the ancient Near East and the language of Jesus.

name: Biblical Hebrew
blurb: Gave English, via the Bible, amen, hallelujah, jubilee and sabbath.

name: Arabic
blurb: Medieval Arabic scholars passed on algebra, algorithm, zero, alcohol, coffee and sugar.

name: Egyptian
blurb: The language of the pharaohs; its descendants gave us ebony, oasis and (probably) gum.

name: Phoenician
blurb: Seafaring traders whose alphabet became ours.

name: Persian
blurb: Gave English paradise, bazaar, caravan, checkmate and pajamas.

name: Sanskrit
blurb: Classical language of India; distant cousin of English. Gave avatar, karma, yoga and guru.

name: Hindi
blurb: Gave English shampoo, bungalow, jungle, loot, pyjamas and thug.

name: Tamil
blurb: One of the world's oldest living languages: curry, catamaran, mango.

name: Malay
blurb: Gave English ketchup (perhaps), amok, orangutan and gong.

name: Chinese
blurb: Gave English tea, ketchup, kowtow and typhoon (in part).

name: Cantonese
blurb: Gave English chop suey, wok, dim sum and kumquat.

name: Japanese
blurb: Gave English tycoon, karaoke, emoji, tsunami and honcho.

name: Ottoman Turkish
blurb: Gave English coffee (via Italian), yogurt, kiosk and tulip.

name: Tagalog
blurb: Gave English boondocks and yo-yo.

name: Russian
blurb: Gave English mammoth, vodka, sputnik and tsar.

name: Czech
blurb: Gave English robot, pistol and polka.

name: Hungarian
blurb: Gave English coach (from the town of Kocs) and paprika.

name: Finnish
blurb: Gave English sauna.

name: Classical Nahuatl
blurb: The language of the Aztecs: chocolate, tomato, avocado, chili and coyote.

name: Quechua
blurb: The language of the Inca: llama, jerky, puma, quinine.

name: Old Tupi
blurb: From Brazil: jaguar, piranha, cashew, toucan.

name: Taíno
blurb: The first American language Europeans met: canoe, hurricane, barbecue, hammock, tobacco.

name: Algonquian languages
blurb: Native languages of eastern North America: moose, raccoon, skunk, moccasin, caucus.

name: Hawaiian
blurb: Gave English ukulele, wiki and aloha.

name: Māori
blurb: Gave English kiwi and haka.

name: Australian Aboriginal languages
blurb: Hundreds of languages; Guugu Yimidhirr gave kangaroo, Dharug gave boomerang, wombat and dingo.

name: Swahili
blurb: Gave English safari and (via Hakuna Matata) a famous motto.

name: Wolof
blurb: West African language; possible source of banana, yam and jive.

name: Bantu languages
blurb: Gave English banjo (probably), gumbo, chimpanzee and zombie.

name: Inuit languages
blurb: Gave English kayak, igloo and anorak.
